transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The U.S. Supreme Court has, for the time being, revived a federal data system the Trump
administration revamped into a tool to check the citizenship of millions of registered
voters.
Here's NPR's Jude Jaffee-Bloch.
The federal tool is called SAVE, and the Trump administration made major changes to it last
year, including linking it to Social Security data for the first time, but the tool has
mistakenly flagged some U.S. citizens as potential non-citizens, leading them to be taken off
state voter rolls as a result.
A federal judge in June said the modified version of SAVE trampled on the privacy rights
of Americans and threatened the right to vote, but the Supreme Court lifted that block and
opened the door for the new SAVE tool to be used in the lead-up to the election for individualized
determinations of citizenship.
Federal law bars systematic purges of voter rolls this close to an election.
Jude Jaffee-Bloch, NPR News.
Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping of China both say they plan to meet two more times before
the end of the year.
America is very happy about this visit, and I'm sure China is very happy also.
Great things for both countries, and it's been just very, very productive.
That's President Trump and Xi here through an interpreter.
The relationship will be a constructive one of strategic stability on the basis of respect,
fairness and reciprocity.
During this week's meetings, both talked about the wars in Iran and Ukraine, as well as Taiwan
and AI, in which Trump and Xi have competing interests, but few details were provided.
New Jersey Governor Mike Sherrill declared a state of emergency in several counties ahead
of a nor'easter that could bring destructive winds and coastal flooding to parts of the
northeastern U.S. starting tonight.
We will surge resources to these communities, making sure that the Department of Environmental
Protection, the Department of Transportation are manning our operations centers because
of beach erosion and the high tide and the roads that we are concerned about.
Concerts and other events have been canceled in parts of New England.
Around a million people in the U.S. live with multiple sclerosis.
Now, new research suggests a common virus is a major culprit, and Piers Ping-Wong reports.
Many people living with MS experience bouts of weakness, vision loss, problems with balance
a few times a year.
Researchers at Mass General Brigham analyzed blood samples from patients and found active
signs of Epstein-Barr virus in the months before these attacks.
Here's Dr. Tanuja Chitnis.
So what we found is that the virus lives inside our B cells, and it's becoming reactivated.
And this was occurring before the attacks.
This virus is very common and doesn't cause MS in most people who get it.
Chitnis says there are likely other genetic and environmental factors that contribute
to the disease.
That's NPR's Ping-Wong reporting.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
A federal judge in Oklahoma handed a win to a Jewish charter school this week.
As State Impact Oklahoma's Beth Wallace reports, this would be the nation's first publicly
funded religious school.
Earlier this year, a state board rejected the application for Ben Gomlet Jewish Charter
School, a virtual school providing religious education.
The board relied on a 2024 Oklahoma Supreme Court ruling for a similar case with a Catholic
school.
Now a judge says that rejection was discriminatory.
Rachel Lazar is the president of Americans United for Separation of Church and State,
which has joined the case.
We're directly funding with taxpayer money, religious education, and turning government
schools into religious government schools.
If appealed, the case could wind up before the U.S. Supreme Court, which was split on
a similar case last year.
For NPR News, I'm Beth Wallace in Tulsa.
A New Mexico jury finds that META misled state residents about its privacy protection policies
and practices on its Facebook platform.
The case involved Cambridge Analytica, the now defunct political consulting firm that
worked on the 2016 Trump presidential campaign and was accused of obtaining data from millions
of Facebook users without their consent.
At trial, META denied its old users' information.
Weekly unemployment claims, a proxy for layoffs, have fallen to their lowest level since mid-July.
The Labor Department has recorded 197,000 applications.
It's NPR.

topics.text: Supreme Court revives federal SAVE tool to check citizenship of registered voters
Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping plan to meet two more times before year end
New Jersey Governor Mike Sherrill declares state of emergency ahead of nor'easter
Research finds Epstein-Barr virus reactivation precedes multiple sclerosis attacks in patients
Federal judge rules Oklahoma rejected Jewish charter school application discriminatorily
New Mexico jury finds META misled residents about Facebook privacy protection policies
Weekly unemployment claims fall to lowest level since mid-July at 197,000
